exposure: in vitro fertilization and embryo transfer (IVF-ET)
outcome: incidence of neonatal complications (very low birth weight, respiratory distress, neonatal hemolysis, hyperbilirubinemia, hypoglycemia, infectious pneumonia, neonatal asphyxia)
physical development at 6 months (weight, head circumference, body mass index, height)
risk factors for perinatal complications (hypertension during pregnancy, placental previa, premature membrane rupture, gestational age <32 weeks, very low birth weight)
cohort: The study included 145 singleton pregnant women conceived via IVF-ET and 160 naturally conceived singleton pregnant women, all delivering at Luohe Central Hospital.
finding: The incidence of perinatal complications was significantly higher in the assisted reproductive technology group, but there were no significant differences in neonatal complications or physical development and NBN scores at 6 months of age compared to naturally conceived singletons.
